title: Marrakech in 3 days: a winter itinerary
author: Matt
intro: Marrakech is one of the warmest city breaks within easy reach of the UK in winter, with sunny days of around 19°C in December. Three days is enough for the medina, the gardens and palaces, and a trip to the Atlas Mountains.
seo_description: Day 1 the medina and souks, day 2 palaces and Jardin Majorelle, day 3 the Atlas Mountains. A 3-day Marrakech plan for winter, with tips for the souks.

sections.heading: Is 3 days enough for Marrakech?
sections.text:
Yes. Three days lets you see the medina, the main palaces and gardens, and spend a day in the Atlas Mountains. Any longer and you might add a night in the desert or a trip to the coast at [Essaouira](/destinations/essaouira).

Winter is a great time to go. December days average about **19°C with plenty of sunshine**, but nights drop to around 6°C, so bring a warm layer. It's far more comfortable for walking than the summer, when temperatures often pass 35°C.

Flights from the UK take about three and a half hours. UK passport holders don't need a visa for stays of up to 90 days, but check the latest GOV.UK advice before you travel.

sections.heading: Day 1: the medina and Jemaa el-Fnaa
sections.text:
Start by getting your bearings in the **medina**, the walled old city:

- **The Koutoubia Mosque.** Its tall minaret is the city's landmark, and a useful way to find your way back. Non-Muslims can't go inside, but the gardens around it are lovely.
- **The souks.** A maze of covered lanes selling leather, lamps, spices, rugs and ceramics. Getting a little lost is part of the experience.
- **Jemaa el-Fnaa.** The main square changes through the day, from juice stalls in the morning to storytellers, musicians and rows of food stalls at night. Eat at the stalls for dinner, or watch from a rooftop café.

Stay in a **riad**, a traditional house built around a courtyard. Many are tucked down quiet lanes in the medina.

sections.heading: Day 2: palaces and gardens
sections.text:
- **Bahia Palace.** A 19th-century palace with painted ceilings, tiled courtyards and gardens.
- **The Saadian Tombs.** Beautifully decorated tombs, rediscovered in the early 20th century. Go early, as the main chamber gets queues.
- **Ben Youssef Madrasa.** A former Islamic school with one of the city's most beautiful courtyards.
- **Jardin Majorelle.** In the afternoon, take a taxi to the new town for this famous garden, with its cobalt-blue villa and cactus beds. It's one of the busiest sights, so **book a timed ticket online** in advance. The YSL Museum is next door.

In the evening, try a traditional hammam, then dinner in Gueliz, the more modern part of the city.

sections.heading: Day 3: the Atlas Mountains
sections.text:
The **High Atlas** is about an hour and a half away, and in winter you'll often see snow on the peaks. Popular day trips include:

- **Imlil**, a mountain village and the starting point for walks with views of Toubkal, North Africa's highest mountain.
- **The Ourika Valley**, with Berber villages and waterfalls.
- **The Agafay Desert**, a rocky desert much closer than the Sahara, for camel rides and sunset dinners.

You can book a guided tour or hire a driver for the day. Pack warm clothes, as it's much colder in the mountains than in the city.

sections.heading: Tips for the souks and the medina
sections.text:
1. **Haggle with a smile.** Prices aren't fixed. Start well below the first price, and be ready to walk away.
2. **Politely ignore unofficial guides.** Some people offer to show you the way, then ask for money or lead you to a shop. A firm "no, thank you" usually works.
3. **Agree taxi fares first**, or ask your riad to book one.
4. **Dress modestly**, covering shoulders and knees, especially in the medina.
5. **Carry some cash.** Morocco uses the dirham. Many small shops and food stalls don't take cards.

Morocco is usually an hour ahead of the UK in winter. During Ramadan, which falls in February and March in 2027, opening hours change and some restaurants close during the day.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.text:
For a short trip, stay inside the medina or just outside its walls. A riad, a traditional house built around a courtyard, is the classic choice: many are small and quiet, serve breakfast on a roof terrace, and can arrange airport transfers, which saves a lot of hassle on arrival. The trade-off is that taxis can't reach most riads, so you may walk the last few minutes through narrow lanes with your bags. Ask whether someone will meet you at the nearest drop-off point.

If you'd rather have a pool and space, the Hivernage and Gueliz districts have larger hotels and wide streets, with the medina a short taxi ride away. Gueliz also has more cafés and restaurants in a modern style, which can be a welcome break after a busy day in the souks.

sections.heading: Getting there and around
sections.text:
There are direct flights to Marrakech from London and several other UK airports. The airport is only a few miles from the medina, about 15 to 20 minutes by taxi. Agree the fare before you get in, or arrange a transfer with your riad.

The medina is best explored on foot, and taxis are cheap for longer trips, for example to Jardin Majorelle or the new town.

sections.heading: If Marrakech isn't quite right
sections.text:
For a quieter Moroccan break, [Essaouira](/destinations/essaouira) is a breezy, walled seaside town, and [Fes](/destinations/fes) has an even older medina. For a longer trip, our [Morocco desert road trip](/destinations/morocco-desert-road-trip) guide goes into the Sahara.

If you're comparing winter sun ideas, our post on [winter sun with no jet lag](/blog/winter-sun-with-no-jet-lag) covers places on UK time or close to it. For other short trips, see [Seville in 3 days](/blog/seville-in-3-days) and our [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page. If your group is split, our guide to [how to decide where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday) can help.

faqs.question: Is 3 days enough in Marrakech?
faqs.answer: Yes. Three days is enough for the medina, the main palaces and gardens, and a day trip to the Atlas Mountains.

faqs.question: Is Marrakech warm in winter?
faqs.answer: Yes, by day. December highs average around 19°C with lots of sunshine, but nights can drop to about 6°C, so bring a warm layer.

faqs.question: Do you need a visa for Morocco from the UK?
faqs.answer: No, UK passport holders can visit Morocco for up to 90 days without a visa. Check the latest GOV.UK travel advice before you go.

faqs.question: Do you need to book Jardin Majorelle in advance?
faqs.answer: It's a good idea. It's one of the busiest sights in Marrakech, and tickets are sold online for timed entry.
